messages:
Oncall-Bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: High TLS handshake failures observed at Cloudflare edge for apis.redwood.com — elevated 5xx (525/526) and connection resets. 30s rolling error rate 11.8% (+9.3ppt). Affected regions: eu-west, us-west. Paging SRE oncall. ticket=INC-2460001
SRE Bot: Incident created INC-2460001 -> Priority: P1. Notifying oncall and ops channels. Runbook: verify origin health, confirm Cloudflare support, consider DNS bypass (set proxied=false) for affected zone.
Amelia W: Ack, oncall here. seeing the spike in Grafana too. latency up ~300ms and many clients reporting TLS errors. Can anyone reproduce from outside CF?
Josh K: I'm seeing handshake failures from multiple CF PoPs when I run openssl against the proxied hostname. example: 
```
$ openssl s_client -servername apis.redwood.com -connect apis.redwood.com:443 -brief
CONNECTED(00000003)
139790567890192:error:14077410:SSL routines:SSL23_GET_SERVER_HELLO:unknown protocol:/build/openssl/ssl/s3_srvr.c:1234
```
Curl from eu-west shows SSL errors and 525 responses: 
```
curl -v https://apis.redwood.com/v1/health
* SSL_connect() failed: SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL in connection to apis.redwood.com:443 
* Closing connection 0
< HTTP/1.1 525 Origin SSL Handshake Error
```
Amelia W: OK that points to CF edge->origin handshake issues or CF presenting wrong cert. Origin itself returns 200 when hit directly (via bastion). Confirming origin: 
```
curl -k https://origin-internal-1.redwood.internal:8443/v1/health
{"status":"ok"}
```
Maria R: Confirmed from our EU probe nodes: errors originate at Cloudflare PoPs. I opened a direct channel to our Cloudflare AM (support ticket #123456). They're investigating SNI mismatch reports.
Josh K: Short-term mitigation options: 1) Reduce TTL and set apis.redwood.com DNS record to DNS-only (proxied:false) to bypass Cloudflare edge -> direct to LB. 2) Turn up retry/backoff in client SDKs (already pushed more tolerant retries for mobile clients). 3) Failover route via backup-cdn (we have backup domain backup-api.redwood.net behind other CDN)
Amelia W: I vote for DNS-only bypass for affected zone. We need to avoid long rollback windows. Maria, can you patch via Cloudflare API and drop proxied flag? Keep TTL low. I'll coordinate with ops to monitor traffic.
Maria R: Executing change now via Cloudflare API (zone id masked). Command: 
```bash
curl -s -X PATCH "https://api.cloudflare.com/client/v4/zones/ZONE_ID/dns_records/RECORD_ID" 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CF_API_TOKEN" 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
  --data '{"type":"A","name":"apis.redwood.com","content":"198.51.100.42","ttl":120,"proxied":false}'
```
Response: {"success":true, "result":{"id":"RECORD_ID","proxied":false}}
SRE Bot: Action logged: CF bypass applied -> apis.redwood.com now DNS-only. Propagation window ~2m (TTL 120). Monitor metrics.
Amelia W: Rolling watchers on Grafana — watch errors, 4xx breakdown, and origin CPU. Also add a temporary rule to LB to accept the increased direct connections.
Ken P: On it. LB connections spike +20% after bypass, origin CPU up but within headroom. Adding an extra origin instance via autoscale group.
Josh K: Also opened a temporary ingress allowlist change for CF IPs no longer proxied so we don’t accidentally block direct client traffic.
Support-Engineer: Noted that external customers reported TLS failures starting ~09:42 UTC. CS ticket queue growing. Sending canned message to cs-team: "We're aware of an ongoing CDN/TLS issue affecting some API requests. We're bypassing Cloudflare to restore reachability and will follow up with full postmortem."
Amelia W: Stats update 09:58 UTC: 5xx rate dropped from 11.8% -> 0.9% after DNS bypass. Latency back to baseline. Marking mitigation: DNS bypass successful. Cloudflare ticket open #123456 — they report internal edge certificate rotation anomalies and are investigating root cause.
Maria R: Cloudflare AM replied: "We see anomalous TLS handshakes from multiple PoPs caused by automated cert rotation. We recommend keeping your domain DNS-only until rotation stabilizes or we finish hotfix." They've escalated to SRE kernel team.
Josh K: I'll prepare a short rollback plan in case we need to re-enable proxied mode: 1) ensure origin auth & WAF rules tested; 2) pre-warm certs in CF UI; 3) schedule small canary shift.
Amelia W: Good. Create incident timeline and set status -> UNDER CONTROL. Add follow-ups: postmortem, certificate hardening, CF account review, add synthetic checks for SNI handshake failures.
SRE Bot: Updated INC-2460001 status: MITIGATED. Notes appended. Follow-ups assigned: certs@infra, cf-account@platform, monitoring@devex.
Ken P: Handoff to night oncall @Ken P at 10:05 UTC. Summary for next oncall: mitigation is in place (DNS-only), CF is investigating automated cert rotation causing handshake failures, origin direct is serving traffic, watch for re-enable plan.
Amelia W: Thanks team. I'll draft an internal postmortem and coordinate with CS for customer communication. :thumbsup:
Support-Engineer: Customer visible update pushed to status.redwood.com: "Partial outage affecting API TLS in EU/US regions — resolved by directing traffic to origin. We are continuing investigation with CDN provider."
Amelia W: Leaving handoff notes in INC-2460001. If Cloudflare requests re-enable proxied mode, don't flip without a low-risk canary.
SRE Bot: Incident INC-2460001 closed for immediate response; postmortem pending.
